system.concept: Tremere enforcer who truly runs Milwaukee's Clan operations
system.biography:
Background

A former CIA assassin Embraced in 1950 after his final mortal target proved to be a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} elder waiting for him, Victor now serves the Clan as its enforcer in Milwaukee. Officially subordinate to Carna on the Council, Victor in truth directs Milwaukee's entire @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} operation: Dr. Mortius reports research needs to him, Victor relays orders to Carna, and Carna's continued good standing with Vienna depends entirely on Victor's reports. He is here to protect the secrecy of the Marquette null-zone investigation and to eliminate any Kindred who tries to seize whatever magic is hidden there for themselves.

Roleplaying Hints

Relaxed and calm on the surface, but radiating quiet menace. Make subtle threats and let hints about your body count do the intimidating rather than open aggression.
system.notes: Sire: Duke Traska. Haven: several, all in wealthy, well-hidden areas. Disciplines as printed: Auspex 3, Dominate 3, Obfuscate 1, Thaumaturgy 3 (capped above to this system's 1-5 scale). Rituals: Defense of Sacred Haven, Wake with Evening's Freshness, Deflection of Wooden Doom, The Watcher, Bladed Hands (the latter two his own creations).

system.description: Maintain physical contact with an object or location and concentrate for a turn, expending a Mental Trait, then ask the Narrator one question about who last touched it, whether it was involved in stressful situations, or what strong emotions drove its user. May be used repeatedly for greater insight; objects of powerful emotional resonance may force a derangement upon the user for the scene.

By this gift, a Toreador may penetrate the "soul" of an inanimate artwork she examines, interpreting the piece, gleaning the artist's state of mind, the relationship between artist and work, and the stages of the creative process, revealed as a series of progressively paler images looking back into the work's history. Some Toreador use this to critique or authenticate a piece; others monitor their proteges' work for unspoken rebellion or sadness, or seek the "real" story behind a letter proposing an alliance. The power does not function on "living" art still in the act of performance — a play, a song, or a story being told — since such work depends on the performer's ongoing intent rather than a fixed, finished creation.

System: The character examines the work and the number of successes determines how much she perceives: a single success yields only general feelings with no historical context; two successes offer a vague sense of the work's history; three successes reveal specific details and a fuzzy timeline; four successes grant a definite sense of the artist's emotional state and a reasonable timeline; five successes let the Toreador see the work in stages, feeling what the artist felt at every step of its creation. The difficulty rises for pieces with multiple artists or a long creation span; examining something as vast as a cathedral or castle risks leaving the Toreador a gibbering wreck from informational overload.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis II: Keepers of the Word, Book One: Artisans (Toreador)

system.description: By winning a Mental Challenge while holding your victim's gaze, you can erase, alter, or implant up to fifteen minutes of memory per challenge, or question the subject to recall details they otherwise might not share.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

system.description: Over several consecutive nights of unrestricted access and repeated Mental Challenges, you can break down a victim's will entirely, turning them into a virtually mindless thrall who obeys you without need for further tests.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

items.name: Thaumaturgy — 2 Intermediate — Command the Freshly Dead

system.description:
The vampire can command any ghost she can see to obey her, receiving answers to questions within the ghost's realm of awareness or sending it to deliver a message. She cannot compel a ghost to perform any task requiring a material form.

System: The vampire must first use See the Dead to locate a desired ghost, then wins a contested Willpower roll against the wraith (most ghosts have 5 Willpower). Each success scored over the wraith's own answers one question or performs one simple action.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis II: Keepers of the Word, Book Two: Usurpers

items.name: Thaumaturgy — 2 Intermediate — Heart of the Wood

system.description:
The vampire may take refuge within the living wood of any tree standing inside her realm of attunement, concealing her presence from enemies; her aura blends with the tree's, increasing the difficulty of detecting her by two Traits' worth of supernatural senses. While inside, she may use Disciplines and abilities not dependent on physical gestures or eye contact. Sheltering within a tree also protects her from the rising sun. If the tree is chopped down she suffers five levels of damage and is forced out; burning the tree inflicts the same damage as aggravated.

System: The vampire drinks a mixture of blood and tree sap, then rolls Willpower. A single success allows her to remain inside a tree for one turn; two successes extend this to a scene; three or more successes let her remain for up to 24 hours, after which the tree ejects her.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis II: Keepers of the Word, Book Two: Usurpers
system.prerequisites: Sielanic Thaumaturgy: Path of the World's Blood; must be attuned to the land

system.description: Once hidden from sight, you may move about at a walk and remain unnoticed, automatically becoming visible only if you speak, make loud noise, or interact with your surroundings.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

vtmlarp.source: Milwaukee by Night, Chapter Three: The Kindred
